title: Recurrent Implantation Failure: Definition, Diagnostic Workup and Evidence-Based Care
subject: ss-reproductive-medicine
refs: ESHRE Working Group Consensus on Recurrent Implantation Failure
ASRM Practice Committee Opinion on Implantation Failure

steps.say: Recurrent implantation failure requires a precise, evidence-based clinical definition. The international ESHRE consensus specifies failure after transferring at least 3 euploid blastocysts or 4 cleavage embryos.
steps.tx: The contemporary **ESHRE definition** classifies **recurrent implantation failure** as the failure to achieve clinical intrauterine pregnancy after transferring at least 3 confirmed **euploid blastocysts** or >=4 good-quality cleavage embryos. Requiring euploid transfers eliminates embryo aneuploidy as the principal confounding explanation for failed attachment.

steps.say: Chronic endometritis represents a common, underdiagnosed cause of implantation failure. Diagnosing this condition requires identifying CD138-positive syndecan-1 plasma cells on endometrial biopsy.
steps.tx: Present in 15 to 30 percent of affected women, subclinical **chronic endometritis** creates persistent mucosal inflammation. Definitive diagnosis requires immunohistochemical staining for **syndecan-1** or **CD138** on endometrial stromal biopsy, identifying infiltrated plasma cells that disrupt normal decidualization. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

nodes.label: Identification of stromal plasma cells confirms diagnosis

steps.say: Oral antibiotic therapy achieves high cure rates for chronic endometritis. First-line management with oral doxycycline at 100 mg twice daily for 14 days delivers over 80 percent histological resolution.
steps.tx: First-line **chronic endometritis treatment** utilizes oral **Doxycycline** administered at 100 mg twice daily for 14 days. This targeted regimen achieves a mucosal **cure rate** exceeding 80 percent, restoring endometrial receptivity and normalizing subsequent pregnancy rates in prospective trials. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

rows: 500 mg PO BID each for 14 days

steps.say: Routine endometrial scratch injury has been disproven by large randomized trials. Performing this procedure in the preceding cycle provides no benefit in live birth rates.
steps.tx: Although widely performed historically, mechanical **endometrial scratch** injury in the preceding luteal phase confers no demonstrable benefit on clinical **live birth rate**. Rigorous multicenter **randomized trial** evidence confirms that routine endometrial injury does not enhance implantation in unselected patients. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

right.title: Randomized Trial Evidence
points: No difference in live birth rates

steps.say: Receptive window displacement explains a subset of implantation failures. Transcriptomic profiling identifies window shifts to guide personalized embryo transfer timing.
steps.tx: A displaced implantation window affects 20 to 25 percent of women with unexplained failure. Employing **transcriptomic profiling** identifies precise **window displacement**, enabling timed **personalized embryo transfer** adjusted by individual progesterone exposure hours to restore optimal synchrony. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

nodes.label: Endometrial biopsy at standard P+5 in HRT cycle
RNA transcriptomic profiling of receptivity genes
Personalized embryo transfer shifted by 12 to 24 hours

steps.say: Refractory thin endometrium poses a difficult clinical challenge. Intrauterine infusions of G-CSF or platelet-rich plasma are used experimentally when lining thickness remains under 7 mm.
steps.tx: When the endometrial stripe fails to reach 7 mm despite high-dose estrogen, clinicians encounter **refractory thin endometrium**. Experimental interventions such as intrauterine infusion of **G-CSF** (300 mcg) or autologous **platelet-rich plasma** aim to stimulate neoangiogenesis and cellular regeneration. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

steps.say: A subclinical hydrosalpinx missed on routine scans impairs blastocyst attachment. Detecting and clipping or removing the diseased tube rectifies the mechanical and toxic implantation defect.
steps.tx: Undetected on routine 2D ultrasound, a **subclinical hydrosalpinx** impairs IVF outcomes through mechanical flushing and embryotoxic reflux. Identifying tubal distension via HSG and performing laparoscopic salpingectomy or proximal **tubal clipping** reverses this profound **implantation defect**. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

left.title: Untreated Hydrosalpinx
points: Doubled rate of early pregnancy loss

steps.say: Popular immunological add-on therapies lack robust scientific backing. Randomized trials provide no proof that intralipid, steroids, or intravenous immunoglobulin improve birth rates.
steps.tx: Clinicians must counsel patients that empirical **immunotherapy add-ons** lack solid scientific validation. High-quality trials evaluating intravenous **intralipid**, prednisolone, and IVIG fail to demonstrate improved live birth rates, with guidelines concluding that **IVIG evidence** does not support routine clinical adoption. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.
